angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 527,341 km at 42.01 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.8052 +/- 0.0125 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 42.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.758 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract): 527,341 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.849 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5192 +/- 61 K from Barber et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of TOI-2076 e's parameter set from Barber et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...32B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barber et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of TOI-2076 e's parameter set from Barber et al. 2025 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170...32B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2076.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.608, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): spectral type K V, from Wang et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD+40 2790: main object type MS*, Main Sequence Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.09 dex, from Osborn et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...664A.156O/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.42285, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): age 0.21 Gyr, from Wang et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026NatAs..10..818W/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): rotation period 7.21 d, from Frazier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...944L..41F/abstract)

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-2076 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 5.27 km/s, from Frazier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...944L..41F/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.758 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.991. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
